tool_input.command: git reset --hard HEAD && echo "=== STATUS AFTER ===" && git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all && echo "(clean if blank above)"

result:
Done. Both parts:

**Discarded the scrap.** All three modified files (`README.md`, `node-slugify/.editorconfig`, `node-slugify/.gitattributes`) had the same junk appended — a `// experiment: <filename>` line. In `.gitattributes` it was actively malformed, and git was emitting `experiment: is not a valid attribute name` on every operation. No untracked files, nothing of value.

One deviation worth flagging: `git reset --hard` is blocked by a guard in this checkout, which pointed at `git stash` instead. I used that rather than overriding. Your working tree is clean either way — the difference is the scrap sits in `stash@{0}` instead of being unrecoverable. Since it's confirmed junk, `git stash drop` clears it for good; I left it in place rather than making that call for you.

**Added the module layout paragraph.** The root README was 4 blank lines, so I gave it a title and a `## Module layout` section. The paragraph is written from reading the source, not the upstream readme:

- `node-slugify/` is the vendored `@sindresorhus/slugify` (ESM-only, Node ≥ 20)
- `index.js` — default `slugify()` plus the stateful `slugifyWithCounter()`
- `index.d.ts` — the `Options` types and per-option examples
- `overridable-replacements.js` — the small `&` → `and` substitution table
- transliteration/regex-escaping delegated to the two runtime deps
- `test.js` runs under AVA + XO; CI covers Node 20 and 24

`git status` now shows only `M README.md`.
